The following MRE shows a problem in the CTI (and VC?) when enum are used

/-
-/
import Veil

veil module bar_mod

type proc
enum msg_req_rsp_type = {idle_r_r,erply,espec,nack,rdsh,rdex,srply,sspec,upack,upgrd,wack,wb,wbbak}

function net_req_rsp_kind : proc → msg_req_rsp_type

after_init {
net_req_rsp_kind P := idle_r_r
}

action p_req (p:proc) {
net_req_rsp_kind p := rdsh
}
--

invariant (net_req_rsp_kind P)=idle_r_r

#time #gen_spec

#check_invariants

end bar_mod

--

I'm using the preview 2.0 branch and I pulled 3pm on June 12 California time

1) You'll notice that rdsh and espec both have the value 2
2) The symbolic name is not used in the Pre-state or the Post-state display, but 1 and 2 instead

Counterexample (TR):
Theory:
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.erply = 0
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.espec = 2
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.idle_r_r = 1
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.nack = 3
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.rdex = 4
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.rdsh = 2
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.srply = 5
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.sspec = 6
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.upack = 7
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.upgrd = 8
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.wack = 9
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.wb = 0
msg_req_rsp_type_Enum.wbbak = 1
Pre-state:
net_req_rsp_kind = [[0, 1]]
Action: p_req(p=0)
Post-state:
net_req_rsp_kind = [[0, 2]]

@Asgeir Eiriksson Thanks for the bug report. It was an issue with Lean SMT's logic for reconstructing uninterpreted sorts rather than an issue in Veil itself. We reported it upstream and fixed it in our fork of Lean SMT.

The latest commit on veil-2.0-preview fixes this. Your example should work after a git pull.

The pull fixed the issue and when I re-ran the test case (that the MRE was derived from) the results changed, i.e. the property that originally exposed the issue now passes (might have pulled some other fixes at the same time?).

The test case above after the pull produces
..
Pre-state:
net_req_rsp_kind = [[0, bar_mod.msg_req_rsp_type_IndT.idle_r_r]]
Action: p_req(p=0)
Post-state:
net_req_rsp_kind = [[0, bar_mod.msg_req_rsp_type_IndT.rdsh]]

Is there a way to not get the bar_mod.msg_req_rsp_type_IndT part? For readability e.g. when I have a couple of pages of these, I want to have the option of only seeing the rdsh part

What does it mean in Veil when a Counterexample (WP) is produced but no Counterexample(TR)?

Is there a way to not get the bar_mod.msg_req_rsp_type_IndT part? For readability e.g. when I have a couple of pages of these, I want to have the option of only seeing the rdsh part

Pushed a fix.

What does it mean in Veil when a Counterexample (WP) is produced but no Counterexample(TR)?

The TR query might have returned unknown.

We have two encodings of verification conditions in Veil. By default, Veil tries to discharge VCs with the weakest-precondition (WP) encoding, which doesn't talk about the post-state. This is usually easier for SMT solvers to tackle.

If the WP VC is disproven, Veil also tries the transition-style (TR) encoding of the VC, so users can look at the post-state as well. If this fails with an error, that's probably a bug in Veil (and you would see an error message in #check_invariants), but if it returns unknown, then the behaviour is simply that no TR counterexample gets displayed.
